final_message:
I've written the stage-2 design to `DESIGN.md`, following the aims-guide steps including the mandatory review-and-revise round, and stopped before any implementation code. I didn't write `QUESTIONS.md`: the product owner's standing instruction in `substrate.md` says to state an assumption and pick a simple reading, and the brief itself settles the one real conflict (a deny anywhere on the path still wins). Nothing is committed.

**Assumptions I stated rather than asked (B1–B5, now in `goals.md`):**
- **B1 – deny always wins:** an explicit deny wins at any level of the hierarchy. So "a more specific grant says otherwise" can only turn an inherited allow into a deny, never the reverse.
- **B2 – the hierarchy is a tree:** each resource has at most one parent, and cycles are rejected when the model is built. A resource not in the hierarchy only gets its own exact grants, and inheritance flows downward only.
- **B3 – windows:** a window is `[from, to)` and either end may be left open. Times must include a timezone; a time without one is an error, never guessed.
- **B4 – `now` is required:** it is a required keyword argument on every question, and the library never reads the clock. The CLI defaults it to the current time and accepts `--now`.
- **B5 – what windows cover:** windows apply to both allow and deny grants. Roles and role assignments are not time-bounded.

**The design:**
- **One owner for "deny wins":** a single private function, `_combine`, is the only code that produces an allow/deny answer. It only receives the set of effects that apply, so it can't see roles, hierarchy levels or time. That means a "most specific grant wins" rule can't sneak in as a small local edit.
- **Everything feeding it only filters:**
  - `decide` gathers across all of the user's roles;
  - each grant checks three things: the action matches exactly, the grant's resource is the asked-about resource or one of its ancestors, and its window contains `now`.
- **Deny is its own value on a grant, not a missing allow.** This matters because if each role returned its own answer, "role X allows, role Y has nothing" would wrongly come out as deny.
- **Stage-1 answers don't change.** With no deny, no hierarchy and no windows, the rule reduces exactly to the stage-1 rule at any `now`; `DESIGN.md` §9.6 has the proof. The in-code `(action, resource)` grant form and every stage-1 JSON file still work unchanged.

**What callers will notice:**
- **Breaking call signature:** an existing `decide(user, action, resource)` call now raises `TypeError`, because `now=` is required. The only way to avoid this would be for the library to read the clock, which B4 rules out.
- **Longer questions on deep hierarchies:** each question walks up the resource's ancestors. I chose this over precomputing every ancestor list, which would cost quadratic memory on deep hierarchies. No performance requirement was stated.

The review round fixed six issues, most importantly a way to build a hierarchy that skipped the cycle check, the quadratic memory cost above, and an architecture test that would have failed on correct code.

Files are in `/home/user/aims-rerun/entitlements`:
- `DESIGN.md`
- `goals.md`
- `decisions/0003-stage2-deny-inheritance-windows.md` (what each draft contributed and why each disagreement was settled the way it was)
- `.aims/state.md`
- `.aims/panel/2026-09-23-stage2/` (the three raw drafts)
